Start application
Apply for funding for a skills hub to deliver high quality, cohort based doctoral training, and design of high-quality postgraduate level taught programmes in fire engineering
EPSRC have up to £5.9 million funding available for this funding opportunity.
As a non-full economic cost award, EPSRC will fund 100% of eligible costs listed in the funding opportunity. Estates and indirect costs will not be funded.
To apply, an expression of interest must be completed by 1 October 2026 at 4:00pm UK time.
Who can apply
This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) individual eligibility rules apply. For full details, visit UKRI’s eligibility page .
Who is eligible to apply
This funding opportunity is only open to higher education institutions.
Organisations can only apply as the lead organisation on one submitted application. However, organisations can be a collaborating organisation or project partner on any number of applications.
The lead organisation:
will play a strategic leadership role in shaping the vision, skills priorities, and delivery model
will lead submission of the application
will act as the training grant holder if you are successful
does not require doctoral research degree awarding powers, but an organisation with these powers must be present within your consortium
must provide the principal base (host) for a minimum of one doctoral student per year of intake for this funding opportunity
Identification of the project lead should not be interpreted as recognition as the dominant partner, where the majority of funds are deployed or where the majority of doctoral studentships will be hosted.
While only one individual can be included as project lead on the UKRI Funding Service, UKRI welcomes applications that reflect flexible and joint leadership models.
EPSRC expects lead organisations to join with additional organisations, forming a consortium, in which other organisations could also host doctoral students or support delivery of the wider skills hub. You are encouraged to engage effectively with other organisations to ensure the:
development of the level 7 (or equivalent) training courses, including continuing professional development training for members of the consortium and potentially shared more widely
delivery of a truly interdisciplinary training environment and experience for doctoral students. Any organisations hosting students must be named as collaborating organisations on your application
Project co-leads are welcome at either the lead organisation or collaborating organisations. Project leads and co-leads may include:
research technical professionals
innovation and commercialisation professionals
research software engineers
professional training and programme managers, where they play an integral role in programme delivery
More information is available on roles in funding applications .
Project partners
Organisations may also act as project partners on your application. Unlike collaborating organisations or subcontractors who can receive funds from the grant, project partners can make direct or indirect contributions to the grant and cannot receive funds from it.
The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government do not require financial contributions from project partners in this funding opportunity but encourage you to develop new or existing links and partnerships with the fire engineering industry and public sector organisations.
Information regarding the nature of these collaborations must be included within your application in the ‘Project partners’ section. Any organisation acting as a project partner may do so on any number of applications, as long as they are able to support them all if funded.
An organisation cannot, on the same application, act as a project partner and as a lead or collaborating organisation.
We welcome applications to include a wide range of project partner organisations contributing to research and skills training. This can include, but is not limited to:
universities that are not leading or co-leading the application
businesses of all scales
public sector organisations, such as public sector research establishments and government at all levels, including devolved administrations
third sector organisations
other key stakeholders across the research and innovation landscape
Your application must demonstrate that there is significant added value from any project partners you choose to form part of your consortium. Examples include:
hosting work experience, placements, venture building activities or similar
co-supervision or mentoring
training for students, programme staff, or both
access to facilities, infrastructure, data, customers or markets
delivery of training, including on entrepreneurship, venture creation or commercialisation
commitment to cover the costs of access to facilities or training that cannot otherwise be provided
strategic links to an important stakeholder or user
supporting employees into doctoral study
There is no limit to the total number of organisations you may include within your application. However, each member of the consortium must make meaningful contributions to the delivery of the training provision, as set out in your application.
International researchers
The UKRI-RCN Money Follows Cooperation Agreement does not apply to this funding opportunity. As such grants submitted to this funding opportunity cannot include a Norway-based project co-lead (international).
You should include all international collaborators (or UK partners not based at approved organisations) as project partners.
Resubmissions
We will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UKRI or any other funder.
Find out more about  EPSRC’s resubmissions policy .
Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
What we're looking for
Demand management
Demand management is being applied to this funding opportunity. Organisations can only apply as the lead organisation on one submitted application.
Aim
The Grenfell Tower Inquiry Phase 2 report makes a number of recommendations relating to the fire engineering profession, which the government has accepted in full, including establishing an independent body to regulate the profession in title and function and to take urgent steps to increase the number of places on master’s level courses.
The government is acting to implement these recommendations. In December 2025, it published the Fire Engineers Advisory Panel’s Authoritative Statement , setting out the knowledge and skills expected of a competent fire engineer. Alongside this, it published the Next steps on fire engineering profession reform setting out the next steps we will take to implement the recommendations concerning fire engineers.
These next steps include how it will increase the fire engineering workforce. In March, we announced £15 million that will make a significant contribution to building the pipeline into the profession.
As part of this package, this funding opportunity provided by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) aims to strengthen the capacity and capability of the fire engineering profession through both education provision and research capability.
EPSRC is one of two delivery partners secured by MHCLG to deliver fire engineering skills development and training. The funding will be distributed by each partner as detailed below:
Royal Academy of Engineering will manage the provision of scholarships for taught Master’s level, innovative routes for future recruitment and other campaigns to enhance the recognition of fire engineering as a profession and attract entrants to the profession
EPSRC is leading the coordination of the allocation of funding for the development of level 7 including continuing professional development (CPD) programmes and doctoral studentships through a skills hub model
A skills hub will develop the skills and capabilities of the next generation of fire engineering practitioners, researchers and innovators.
It will address the skills gaps and differing levels of training provision across the UK Fire Engineering community and adjacent professions.
It will provide leadership in research, through the funding of new doctoral studentships, and will coordinate and support the development of new and updated level 7 provision for training master’s students, doctoral students and supporting the wider continuing professional development of the UK fire engineering community.
Scope
The funding is provided as part of the UK government Building Workforce programme designed to increase capacity and capability of safety critical professions which includes fire engineering.
There are three elements for the skills and training provided by this funding:
a doctoral training programme to support the next generation of researchers in fire engineering through a cohort based, highly tailored training programme
the development of taught postgraduate (level 7) development programmes for the fire engineering community with innovative modes of study to cater for a range of audiences
the development of level 7 fire engineering continuing professional development training for the wider fire engineering community and adjacent professions wishing to upskill or re-train into fire engineering
You must deliver all the above elements.
We welcome applications from multi organisational consortia which bring together expertise in fire engineering. Consortia can be new collaborations, as well as applications that expand on existing doctoral training investments. Cohesion across the consortium must be demonstrated in the application, including a clear case for the given size of their consortia.
You will be expected to work in collaboration with the ongoing work:
to underpin future regulation and reform of the fire engineering profession
of the regulator responsible for the accreditation of education programmes
You are expected to:
deliver specialist fire engineering teaching capacity with recognition given to the government’s commitment to fire safety strategy being the central, protected function of the profession
provide emphasis on the ethical practice fundamental to ensuring life safety
demonstrable fire engineering research capability sufficient to support research-led teaching, dissertation supervision, and engagement with emerging fire safety challenges, including the ability to contribute to the future development of the profession
deliver assessment of students’ ability to apply fire engineering knowledge to realistic design, risk and regulatory scenarios
provide evidence that students develop skills necessary to work effectively within multidisciplinary design, construction and regulatory environments
show clear routes towards accreditation or professional recognition
develop meaningful links with industry, professional bodies, and the fire sector
demonstrate credible plans for financial sustainability including plans beyond the funding period
evidence that provision will widen access across geography, career stage (including accessibility for those in work), and student background
In addition, support should prioritise courses that align with the Fire Engineers Advisory Panel’s Authoritative Statement . The proposed skills hub should provide foundational scientific and engineering knowledge alongside specific learning in fire engineering principles and practice. This should include the development and stewardship of the fire safety strategy, ethical professional conduct, fire dynamics, prevention, human behaviour, building structures, systems and operations, fire-fighting needs, and good analytical and communication skills.
Doctoral training programme
Expectations for the doctoral training element of this funding opportunity will include the following:
to support up to two cohorts on a four-year doctorate, bringing together a critical mass of academic and industrial supervisors of internationally recognised research excellence with a track record of doctoral supervision
for the one to two skills hubs funded we expect to support at least 18 students
entrants onto the doctoral training programme should normally have completed a masters (MEng or MSc) or equivalent qualification in a relevant engineering or scientific discipline. The degree must be accredited by the Engineering Council or an equivalent body
to develop a cohort approach to doctoral education including peer-to-peer learning, within the cohort. Students may also work as a cohort to address research challenges
to nurture a diverse and inclusive research environment to support people in achieving world class research
to provide opportunities for significant, challenging, and original research projects leading to the award of a doctoral-level degree in accordance with a university’s standard regulations. Universities are free to choose the type of research doctoral qualification that is offered to students, for example PhD or EngD. You may choose to offer all students the same type of qualification or a mixture, and to consider innovative approaches to delivering, awarding and assessing doctoral degrees
students should also expect that doctoral projects are designed or planned in such a way that (barring exceptional circumstances) they are able to submit their thesis within their four-year funded period or part-time equivalent
where needed, consider the delivery of suitable, taught activities which would develop and enhance, for example, technical disciplinary and multidisciplinary knowledge, as well as broadening skills including, for example, project management, entrepreneurship and commercialisation
to embed a culture of responsible research and innovation, environmental sustainability, equality, diversity and inclusion, trusted research approaches and support for student wellbeing to the highest standard
to provide opportunities for students to engage with industrial and government stakeholders, for example in the form of joint supervision, industrial placements or expert advice and input. This could also take the form of the co-creation of doctoral projects. The training should maximise the impact from this investment and grow capacity in this area for the benefit of the nation. If pursuing industrial placements, the management team will need to ensure students are given sufficient time to complete their doctoral studies
as appropriate, to provide innovative approaches to doctoral study. This may include support for students who are based in non-academic organisations for the majority of their time, either receiving a stipend or by contributing to their salary. Where beneficial for the research area, student or project partner, we expect applicants to build on routes such as engineering doctorates and the innovative approaches in EPSRC centres for doctoral training, doctoral training partnership mobility pilots, or other recent UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) training investments
to create opportunities for supervisors and students to identify and align synergies between individual doctoral projects so that the sum of the activity is greater than its component parts
to support mechanisms, where appropriate, by which students can reach out to the broader research community, user community and wider public
to add value to the UK’s existing landscape by working with other large investments to develop an integrated network of research, innovation and skills capability
to provide appropriate access to a wide range of equipment, facilities and e-infrastructure, for example, software and high-performance computing. Students should benefit from the environment and accessibility of infrastructure at the hosting institutions and partners. If appropriate to their research, students should also have access to large facilities and UKRI national research facilities
While not an exclusive list, the areas of skills for doctoral research could include:
fire safety strategy
egress modelling of evacuation lifts
advancing instrumentation for external wall fire testing
a decision framework for identifying and managing built environment risks
the role of smouldering in fire safety design for mass timber structures
from disaster to foresight: a framework for identifying future building safety threats
fire resistance and structural resilience in modern methods of construction
understanding the long-term performance of fire-retardant treatments
Postgraduate-level 7 including continuing professional development (CPD) programme development
The funding provided for the post-graduate (level 7) programmes including CPD programme development is intended to coordinate and support, across the collaborating institutions of the skills hub, the development of new and the updating of existing level 7 standalone taught master’s programmes or shorter courses. Provision should include modules for master’s or part-master’s (PG Cert, PD Dip) level, micro-credentials, stand-alone modules to support the CPD of those in employment.
The funding is also intended to support the upskilling and level 7 CPD of existing professionals in employment in the UK fire engineering sector or other related disciplines, including bridging and conversion modules. Bridging modules and conversion pathways aimed at those who have studied or are working in related disciplines, for example:
mechanical engineering
structural engineering
civil engineering
architecture
building services engineering
physics, construction management.
Both postgraduate-level 7 including CDP programmes must be credit-bearing and include some form of assessment.
Duration
Applications must have a maximum duration of 60 months with respect to doctoral training. The post-graduate (level 7) programmes including CPD programme development funding must be spent by end of March 2029.
For doctoral studentships only
Where the end date of an individual studentship is subsequently extended later than the end date of the grant, in line with training grant conditions six and eight, award holders will be able to apply to EPSRC at the time to extend the grant, which may be beyond 60 months. Projects must start no earlier than 1 April 2027 and no later than 1 October 2027. Awards will have a fixed start date, on the date requested in the application.
Funding available
£5.9 million funding in total is available to support up to two skills hubs delivering a combination of doctoral training, level 7 post-graduate development programmes including CPD training programmes.
Applicants requesting the full £5.9 million available must demonstrate coverage of the full scope of this funding opportunity and include key institutions delivering post graduate training in fire engineering.
As a training grant (non-full economic cost award), EPSRC will fund 100% of eligible costs listed in the opportunity. Eligible costs vary between EPSRC training grants, so please check the ‘What we will fund’ and ‘What we will not fund’ sections for full details.
All costs (including stipends and fees) requested in applications should be calculated at your chosen October 2026 rates with no addition made to consider inflation over the length of the funding period. This includes the appropriate fee rate for your institution(s) and any enhanced stipend rates above the UKRI minimum, described below. UKRI will include an allowance for fee and stipend indexation at the final funding stage.
What we will fund
Doctoral training
We will fund doctoral studentship costs up to a maximum of the equivalent of 18 students. This could be, for example, 100% funding for 18 students or 50% funding for 36 students.
Students will be funded across a maximum of two cohorts.
Applications must specify the number of students that will be supported. This should align to the proposed delivery model and costs per studentship proposed in the application.
Please complete the costings template. Justifications for costs, numbers of students, durations of studentships will be examined carefully to ensure value for money.
UKRI funding for studentship costs includes the following.
Tuition fees
Fees charged to UKRI cannot be higher than the fee charged by the university for home funded students on similar programmes.
UKRI’s standard 30% cap on international students will apply.
Stipends
The stipends must be at least at the minimum rates published by UKRI. We will not cover additional college fees. You are encouraged to request funding for enhanced stipends, where justified, to attract UK home students in the context of the area of research and training and UK skills need.
Given the importance of establishing increased capability and research capacity in fire engineering in the UK, you may, for example, choose to set stipends comparable to the HESA graduate outcomes survey salary data for engineering and technology, adjusted to an October 2026 equivalent and taking into account that the stipend is not taxed. EPSRC’s estimate of this is £29,500 or £7,500 above the UKRI minimum.
Stipend support will also be covered for doctoral candidates based for the majority of their time in a company, or other non-academic organisation. If you are proposing more innovative options, such as contributions to salaries, you are encouraged to contact EPSRC before submission, to discuss the best route to fund this. You must ensure at all times that training grant funding is compliant with the Subsidy Control Act 2022.
Research training support grant (RTSG)
This covers items for individual students such as travel, consumables, and facility access where this is linked to conducting the research of the project, or specialised training such as a summer school only being attended by a student due to their project.
As well as the studentship costs above, we will also fund other costs including:
leadership and management costs, where these are specific and proportionate to the delivery of the award
direct costs that are explicitly linked to training activities and student development
additional support needed to facilitate diversity and mobility of career paths, and to accommodate doctoral students at different career stages or employed in relevant industrial sectors
wider career development experience for students
innovative routes for student recruitment and widening the participation of underrepresented groups in doctoral study
Postgraduate-level 7 including CPD programme development
We will fund the following costs with respect to postgraduate level 7 including CPD programme development:
academic and technical experts time for the proposed programme development
leadership and management costs, where these are specific and proportionate to the delivery of the award
lab time and the cost of equipment to support the delivery of research-oriented taught programmes (not pure research) to a maximum value of £400,000 per consortium. Funding for equipment covers items between £25,000 and £400,000. Items under £25,000 are not considered equipment
If successful you will have flexibility in how you use the funding awarded and we encourage flexibility and virement between headings, subject to the standard UKRI terms and conditions for training grants . The only exception will be where UKRI makes separate awards to lead and collaborating organisations to reflect subsidy control considerations, where there will be limitations on viring across separate awards.
What we will not fund
We will not fund the following costs:
direct costs associated with applying for intellectual property (IP) protection (including patent filing costs)
costs associated with student supervision
visa and international health surcharge costs for international students
estates and indirect costs
Supporting skills and talent
We encourage you to follow the principles of the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers and the Technician Commitment .
Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI)
EDI is a core feature of this funding opportunity, in line with UKRI’s principles on EDI . We want to work with our partners to shape a dynamic, diverse, and inclusive system of research and innovation that is an integral part of society.
Your doctoral training programme should work to provide everyone involved with an opportunity to participate in, and benefit from, the award.
You should provide a brief summary at the application stage of how your EDI strategy will embed the core principles of EDI at all levels and across all aspects of the award, including:
increasing access to doctoral study, including recruitment
working practices, including individualised student support
wellbeing support, including mental health
monitoring and evaluation, including a baseline and plans for improvement
We will require successful applicants to develop detailed EDI strategies, activities and commitments. These will be regularly reviewed by UKRI. Data will be collected on at least a yearly basis via annual reports, and we will reserve the right to access these data across the lifetime of the award. For more information see the UKRI data collection policy .
You should also refer to  equality, diversity and inclusion at UKRI  and EPSRC EDI action plan 2026 to 2029 .
Legacy and impact
Training programmes which are supported by this funding opportunity are done so with the intention of developing a legacy of training excellence. Applications must demonstrate consideration of the legacy and impacts of the doctoral training programme beyond the lifetime of the UKRI investment.
Reporting requirements and monitoring
We expect award holders to monitor progress towards the vision and objectives of your programme, as well as evidence impact from this investment.
This information will be used by EPSRC to review the success of our training investments. Information provided will also be used to provide assurance that awards are being managed appropriately and are progressing in accordance with the original funding application. This will be conducted in various ways, including:
mandatory annual reports
a mid-term review of progress
hosting a regular visit by EPSRC staff
Successful applicants will be expected to respond to other reporting requirements when requested.
We will use key information required from the training programmes supported by this funding opportunity in reports and publications.
You are expected to describe your approach to monitoring and evaluation, outlining your success measures and baselines and a continuous improvement process built in within your applications.
Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I)
UKRI is committed in ensuring that effective international collaboration in research and innovation takes place with integrity and within strong ethical frameworks. Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I) is a UKRI work programme designed to help protect all those working in our thriving and collaborative international sector by enabling partnerships to be as open as possible, and as secure as necessary. Our TR&I Principles set out UKRI’s expectations of organisations funded by UKRI in relation to due diligence for international collaboration.
As such, applicants for UKRI funding may be asked to demonstrate how their proposed projects will comply with our approach and expectation towards TR&I, identifying potential risks and the relevant controls you will put in place to help proportionately reduce these risks.
See further guidance and information about TR&I , including where applicants can find additional support.
How to apply
Expression of interest (EoI)
This funding opportunity has a mandatory EOI stage. This will enable EPSRC to prepare for the assessment process. Any applications without an EOI will be rejected.
Please submit your EOI via  Citizen Space . The deadline for submission of an EOI is 1 October 2026 at 4:00pm UK time.
The EOI should include:
contact details for the project lead
contact details for others involved in the application, including a contact for the lead organisation’s research office
the title of your proposed fire engineering skills hub
other organisations that are expected to be involved in delivering the skills hub, including the lead organisation and any confirmed or likely collaborating organisations
the thematic areas your training programme will cover (approximately 200 words)
Only the lead organisation should submit an EOI. Universities must discuss with their university research office before submitting an EOI.
Your EOI will not be assessed externally. It will be used by EPSRC to plan the assessment process. We will only contact you if we require any clarifications or have any concerns about whether the proposed work is in scope and remit for this funding opportunity. We intend to publish the details of the project lead, lead institution, institutions involved in the consortium and the summary provided of each expression of interest.
Only applications that have submitted an EOI will be permitted to submit a full application.
Full proposals stage
We are running this funding opportunity on the new UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Funding Service, so please ensure that your organisation is registered. You cannot apply on the Joint Electronic Submissions (Je-S) system.
The project lead is responsible for completing the application process on the Funding Service, but we expect all team members and project partners to contribute to the application.
Only the lead research organisation can submit an application to UKRI. Please refer to the eligibility sections on the UKRI website to ensure that your organisation and applicants are eligible for UKRI funding. Check if your organisation is eligible .
To apply
Select ‘Start application’ near the beginning of this Funding finder page:
Confirm you are the project lead.
Sign in or create a Funding Service account. To create an account, select your organisation, verify your email address, and set a password.
Answer questions directly in the text boxes. You can save your answers and come back to complete them or work offline and return to copy and paste your answers. If we need you to upload a document, follow the upload instructions in the Funding Service. All questions and assessment criteria are listed in the How to apply section on this Funding finder page.
Allow enough time to check your application in ‘read-only’ view before sending to your research office.
Send the completed application to your research office for checking. They will return it to you if it needs editing.
Your research office will submit the completed and checked application to UKRI.
Please be aware that research office and finance teams undertake checks on hosting arrangements and financial eligibility. The ultimate responsibility for ensuring compliance with all opportunity requirements lies with the applicant.
Where indicated, you can also demonstrate elements of your responses in visual form if relevant.
When including images, you must:
provide a descriptive caption or legend for each image immediately underneath it in the text box (this must be outside the image and counts towards your word limit)
insert each new image onto a new line
use files smaller than 5MB and in JPEG, JPG, JPE, JFI, JIF, JFIF, PNG, GIF, BMP or WEBP format
Images should only be used to convey important visual information that cannot easily be put into words. The following are not permitted, and your application will be rejected if you include:
sentences or paragraphs of text
tables
excessive quantities of images
A few words are permitted where the image would lack clarity without the contextual words, such as a diagram, where text labels are required for an axis or graph column.
For more guidance on the Funding Service, see:
how applicants use the Funding Service
how research offices use the Funding Service
how reviewers use the Funding Service
References
References should be included within the word count of the appropriate question section. You should use your discretion when including references and prioritise those most pertinent to the application.
Hyperlinks can be used in reference information. When including references, you should consider how your references will be viewed and used by the assessors, ensuring that:
references are easily identifiable by the assessors
references are formatted as appropriate to your research
persistent identifiers are used where possible
General use of hyperlinks
Applications should be self-contained. You should only use hyperlinks to link directly to reference information. You must not include links to web resources to extend your application. Assessors are not required to access links to conduct assessment or recommend a funding decision.
Generative artificial intelligence (AI)
Use of generative AI tools to prepare funding applications is permitted, however, caution should be applied.
For more information see our policy on the  use of generative AI in application and assessment .
Deadline
EPSRC must receive your application by 3 November 2026 at 4:00pm UK time.
You will not be able to apply after this time.
Make sure you are aware of and follow any internal institutional deadlines.
Following the submission of your application to this funding opportunity, your application cannot be changed, and submitted applications will not be amended. If your application does not follow the guidance, it may be rejected.
If an application is withdrawn prior to peer review or office rejected due to substantive errors in the application, it cannot be resubmitted to the opportunity.
Personal data
Processing personal data
EPSRC as part of UKRI, will need to collect some personal information to manage your Funding Service account and the registration of your funding applications.
We will handle personal data in line with UK data protection legislation and manage it securely. For more information, including how to exercise your rights, read our privacy notice .
EPSRC, as part of UKRI, will need to share the application and any personal information that it contains with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and the Royal Academy of Engineering so that they can participate in the assessment process.
For more information on how personal information is used visit the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (PDF, 107KB) and the Royal Academy of Engineering .
Sensitive information
If you or a core team member need to tell us something you wish to remain confidential, email TFSchangeEPSRC@epsrc.ukri.org
Include in the subject line: [the funding opportunity title; sensitive information; your Funding Service application number].
Typical examples of confidential information include:
individual is unavailable until a certain date (for example due to parental leave)
declaration of interest
additional information about eligibility to apply that would not be appropriately shared in the ‘Applicant and team capability’ section
conflict of interest for UKRI to consider in reviewer or panel participant selection
the application is an invited resubmission
For information about how UKRI handles personal data, read UKRI’s privacy notice .
Institutional matched funding
There is no requirement for matched funding from the institutions hosting the project lead, project co-leads or other staff employed on the application, beyond costs that are not eligible. Expert reviewers and panels assessing UKRI funding applications must not consider levels of institutional matched funding as a factor on which to base recommendations.
This policy does not remove the need for support from host organisations who must provide the necessary research environment and infrastructure for award-specific activities funded by UKRI. For example, research facilities, training and development of staff.
Publication of outcomes
EPSRC, as part of UKRI, will publish the outcomes of this funding opportunity at EPSRC Funding Applications Outcomes
If your application is successful, we will publish some personal information on the UKRI Gateway to Research .
Summary
Word limit: 550
In plain English, provide a summary we can use to identify the most suitable experts to assess your application.
We usually make this summary publicly available on external-facing websites, therefore do not include any confidential or sensitive information. Make it suitable for a variety of readers, for example:
opinion-formers
policymakers
the public
the wider research community
Guidance for writing a summary
Clearly describe your proposed work in terms of:
context
the challenge the project addresses
aims and objectives
potential applications and benefits
Core team
List the key members of your team and assign them roles from the following:
project lead (PL)
project co-lead (UK) (PcL)
specialist
grant manager
professional enabling staff
research and innovation associate
technician
visiting researcher
researcher co-lead (RcL)
Only list one individual as project lead.

Funding opportunity
Funding opportunity: Pre-announcement: ESRC applicant-led: grow awards
Opportunity status:
Upcoming
Funders:
Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)
Funding type:
Grant
Award range: £100,000 - £500,000
Publication date:
8 September 2026
Opening date:
5 November 2026 9:00am UK time

Open - no closing date
Apply for funding to build the skills, experience and confidence to make a step-change in your research career. Grow awards support individuals at key career points to develop new capabilities or pivot in a new direction, strengthening the long-term capacity, adaptability and resilience of the UK’s social science research base.
You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for ESRC funding.
The full economic cost (FEC) of your project can be up to £500,000. ESRC will fund 80% of the FEC. Projects can last between 18 months and five years.
This is a pre-announcement and the information may change. More information will be available on this page when the funding opportunity opens.
Who can apply
This opportunity will be open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
Who can apply
You can be at any stage of your career. Grow awards must focus on the development of the project lead. Other members of the project team are permitted if their contributions are required for the development project.
There is no limit to the number of additional roles that can be added. All members of the project team must be fully justified and meet the requirements set out in the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) roles in funding applications .
International researchers can apply as project co-lead (international) . You must include all other international collaborators (or UK partners not based at approved organisations) as project partners.
Business, third sector or government body project co-leads based in the UK can also be included as a project co-lead.
We welcome applications that take an interdisciplinary approach. Find out more about how UKRI supports research that spans different disciplines .
The social sciences within ESRC’s remit must represent more than 50% of the research focus and effort. Complete and submit the remit query form , if you are unsure whether your proposed research falls within ESRC’s remit.
Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
What we're looking for
Demand management
We do not anticipate that demand management will be applied to this funding opportunity.  However, should the level of interest exceed what can be managed within the assessment process, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) may introduce limits on the number of applications that can be submitted. Further details will be clearly communicated where this is the case. UKRI encourages organisations to support applicants in preparing well-planned, high-quality applications that are competitive for funding relative to the funding opportunity.
Aim
A strong and internationally competitive social science research base is built on researchers having opportunities to develop new capabilities or pursue novel directions so they can maximise their full career potential. Grow awards enable researchers at three key career development and transition points to meaningfully strengthen or redirect their skills and experience:
those establishing their independence as researchers
those pivoting to a new social science discipline in a bold way
those developing expertise in advanced or emerging methods, technologies or approaches needed to drive innovation in their field. This development of individuals will enhance the long-term capacity, adaptability and resilience of the UK’s social science research base
Scope
Grow awards support researchers to make a meaningful step-change in their skills, experience and expertise in ways that can open up new opportunities for their field as well as support their individual career development. You will be looking to establish independence at an early research career stage, move within or into social science disciplines in a novel way, or build methodological and technical capabilities to support innovation in their field. By unlocking your potential to lead work that is new to you at these key career development points, Grow awards will help build a dynamic, flexible and internationally competitive UK social science research base.
You must set out a defined project through which you will develop, deploy and test the skills needed to meet your development objectives. There is no prescribed model, and we expect the mix of research, training and skills development proposed to be tailored specifically to your development needs, your project objectives, and its wider potential significance. We welcome proposals across a wide range of funding scales and award durations. You have the freedom to propose the approach that best achieves your aims. That could include a research or data analysis project, collaboration or mentoring, placement or other form of immersion, skills or methodological development activity, or another route.
What a high-quality project involves will differ between those at the start of their research career and those at more established stages who are looking to significantly shift focus or upskill. What defines a Grow award is not the focus or form of the development activity proposed but its potential for meaningful impact on both the individual researcher’s skills and capabilities at a key career point and its potential for contributing to the wider capacity, adaptability and resilience of the UK’s social science research base.
Duration
The duration of this award is between 18 and 60 months.
Funding available
The FEC of your project can between £100,000 and £500,000.
ESRC will fund 80% of the FEC.
What we will fund
You must set out plans for skills development appropriate to your objectives. You should propose a defined project through which you will develop, deploy and test those skills in ways that support your career progression and have potential to contribute to the wider capacity, adaptability and resilience of UK social science. There is no prescribed model for the development activity or project, and we expect the approach to be tailored specifically to the individual applicant and the project objectives.
You have wide scope and freedom to propose the activities most suitable to meet your project’s objectives. Activities might include but are not limited to:
basic or applied research projects that enable career development objectives
secondary analysis and other forms of existing data reuse that enable career development objectives
methodological or technical capability development and application
interdisciplinary collaborations and transfer of insights or techniques across disciplinary boundaries
discipline transitions within (or into) the social sciences
placements, secondments or immersive development opportunities in both academic and non-academic contexts
tailored mentoring or leadership development activities
All activity funded under Grow must be accompanied by plans that articulate how the award will have a demonstrable effect on career progression, and how the wider potential benefit to the UK’s social science research base will be maximised.
What we will not fund
Applications cannot be accepted under this funding opportunity for:
uninvited resubmissions of projects that have previously been submitted to UKRI. Find out more about UKRI’s resubmissions policy
unspecified research work
research already underway or carried out
writing up previous research or completing previously funded research objectives
general literature reviews not related to the proposed development project
general conference attendance, not related to the proposed development project
travel for general study not related to the proposed development project
expeditions not related to the proposed development project
requests to hold conferences, workshops or seminars where these constitute the primary project component.
preparation of books and publications not related to the proposed development project
preparation and production of materials such as curriculum materials and software development where these constitute the primary project component
training courses or learning activities where these constitute the primary project component
research, evidence synthesis, or knowledge exchange activity with no associated development component
transitions to disciplines outside the social sciences
transitions to research-focused or other roles in non-academic organisations
transitions to non-research roles within academic organisations
The following cannot be included in applications:
flexible funding pots that enable subcontracting of further small research projects
Host organisation support
We expect the host research organisation to support the applicant in their individual development objectives as outlined in the application. This may include both mentoring support and a programme of research and skills development as appropriate to the proposed application outcomes. There is no prescribed model, and we expect the support package to be tailored specifically to the individual applicant and the application objectives. This will need to be fully articulated and justified in the application. There is no requirement for matched funding from the institutions hosting the project lead, project co-leads or other staff employed on the application, beyond the standard 20% FEC.
Supporting skills and talent
We encourage you to follow the principles of the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers and the Technician Commitment .
Research ethics
We require that the research we support is designed and conducted in such a way that it meets ethical principles and is subject to proper professional and institutional oversight in terms of research governance. We have agreed a Framework for Research Ethics that all submitted proposals must comply with. Read further details about the Framework for Research Ethics and guidance on compliance.
ESRC data infrastructure
We support a range of data infrastructure. You must carefully consider how your project can use, build on or contribute to existing data resources and infrastructures, where appropriate.  See Facilities and resources for information on finding and using ESRC datasets which are available across the UK.
Data requirements
We recognise the importance of data quality and provenance. Data generated, collected or acquired by ESRC-funded research must be well-managed by the grant holder to enable their data to be exploited to the maximum potential for further research. See our research data policy for details and further information on data requirements . The requirements of the research data policy are a condition of ESRC research funding.
Where relevant, details on data management and sharing should be provided in the Data Management section. See the importance of managing and sharing data and content for inclusion in a data management plan on the UK Data Service (UKDS) website for further guidance. We expect applicants to provide a summary of the points provided.  The UKDS (email: datasharing@ukdataservice.ac.uk ) will be pleased to advise you on the availability of data within the academic community and provide advice on data deposit requirements.
Equitable partnership principles
When undertaking research and innovation activities outside the UK, you must recognise and address the possible impact of contextual, societal and cultural differences on the ethical conduct of those activities.
Researchers should also follow the principles of equitable partnerships to address inherent power imbalances when working with partners in resource-poor settings.
Applying the principles will encourage equitable access, especially in low and middle-income countries , while maintaining incentives for innovation. You should consider the principles from the start of the research and development cycle.
Read UKRI’s guidance on research in a global setting .
Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I)
UKRI is committed in ensuring that effective international collaboration in research and innovation takes place with integrity and within strong ethical frameworks. Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I) is a UKRI work programme designed to help protect all those working in our thriving and collaborative international sector by enabling partnerships to be as open as possible, and as secure as necessary. Our TR&I Principles set out UKRI’s expectations of organisations funded by UKRI in relation to due diligence for international collaboration.
As such, applicants for UKRI funding may be asked to demonstrate how their proposed projects will comply with our approach and expectation towards TR&I, identifying potential risks and the relevant controls you will put in place to help proportionately reduce these risks.
See further guidance and information about TR&I , including where you can find additional support.
How to apply
We are running this funding opportunity on the new UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Funding Service, so please ensure that your organisation is registered. You cannot apply on the Joint Electronic Submissions (Je-S) system. We will publish full details on how to apply when the funding opportunity opens.
Institutional matched funding
There is no requirement for matched funding from the institutions hosting the project lead, project co-leads or other staff employed on the application, beyond the standard 20% FEC. Expert reviewers and panels assessing UKRI funding applications must not consider levels of institutional matched funding as a factor on which to base recommendations. Direct and in-kind contributions from third party project partners are encouraged.
This policy does not remove the need for support from host organisations who must provide the necessary research environment and infrastructure for award-specific activities funded by UKRI. For example, research facilities, training and development of staff.

Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I)
Trusted Research and Innovation is the protection of the UK’s intellectual property, sensitive research, people, and infrastructure from potential theft, misuse, and exploitation.
Organisations receiving UKRI funding are obliged to act in line with UK government legislation. They are also expected to undertake appropriate due diligence assessments of organisations involved in research partnerships, collaboration agreements, and commercial contracts.
You will be asked about:

How we will assess your application
Assessment process
We will assess your application using the following process.
Eligibility checks will be carried out by ESRC at the point of submission on applicants, named staff and the application’s fit to the funding opportunity criteria. Applications which do not meet these will be rejected.
We will invite at least three expert reviewers to independently assess each application on its own merit against the funding opportunity criteria. These may be drawn from the ESRC Peer Review College or other sources. You will not be able to nominate reviewers. If your application does not receive sufficient support in scores or comments from the first two reviews it may be rejected before a third review is sourced.
If your application secures sufficient support from expert reviewers, you will be able to respond to the reviewer comments. Your application will then be considered by an appropriate ESRC applicant-led moderating panel. Panel members will use your application, the expert reviews and your response to confirm its quality against the funding opportunity requirements and provide a final score. Applications will be assessed on individual merit and will not be ranked relative to each other.
ESRC will make the final funding decision, using a tiered approach. The final funding decision may adopt a portfolio approach to ensure a diverse range of projects in accordance with  How we make decisions ; balancing novelty, research significance, approach and impact potential in a way that is appropriate to the opportunity aims.
We reserve the right to adapt our assessment process should we receive a large volume of applications.
Timescale
You should apply when your application is ready for submission. We will hold regular decision points and will initiate the assessment process once an application is received, ensuring you receive a timely decision.
Feedback
Applications will receive expert reviewer comments as feedback. Additional feedback will not be available. For applications that proceed to panel, the score range will be available on our website once the decisions for the opportunity have been processed fully.
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco declaration on research assessment and recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Find out about the UKRI principles of assessment and decision making .
Using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in expert review
Generative AI may only be used for the purpose of language refinement during application assessment. When using generative AI to refine the language of a review, expert reviewers and panellists must ensure that:
no part of the application being assessed is entered into a generative AI tool
no personal information from the application is disclosed
generative AI is not tasked with understanding, summarising or evaluating the application’s content
Expert reviewers and panellists must also:
comply with relevant intellectual property and data protection legislation
not take into account or speculate within their assessment whether generative AI has been used to develop the application
For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI .

resources and cost justification

Apply for funding to advance knowledge through ambitious, curiosity-driven social science. We are looking for creative, innovative and bold proposals within ESRC’s remit that advance knowledge by pushing disciplinary, methodological or conceptual boundaries. You can propose the approach that best achieves your aims. We will fund individuals or research teams with up to four core members.
You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for ESRC funding.
The full economic cost (FEC) of your project can be up to £2 million. ESRC will fund 80% of the FEC. Projects can last up to five years.
This is a pre-announcement and the information may change. More information will be available on this page when the funding opportunity opens.
Who can apply
This opportunity will be open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
Who can apply
You can be at any stage of your career.
Applications must be submitted by an individual researcher or a small central research team consisting of no more than four members, comprising one project lead and up to three project co-leads.
Further research and innovation associates, grant managers, specialists, technicians and professional enabling staff can be included in addition, so long as their contributions are fully justified and meet the requirements set out in the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) roles in funding applications .
International researchers can apply as project co-lead (international) and must be included within the maximum team size. You must include all other international collaborators (or UK partners not based at approved organisations) as project partners.
Business, third sector or government body project co-leads based in the UK can also be included as a project co-lead and must be included within the maximum team size.
We welcome applications that take an interdisciplinary approach. Find out more about how UKRI supports research that spans different disciplines .
The social sciences within ESRC’s remit must represent more than 50% of the research focus and effort. Complete and submit the remit query form , if you are unsure whether your proposed research falls within ESRC’s remit.
Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
What we're looking for
Demand management
We do not anticipate that demand management will be applied to this funding opportunity. However, should the level of interest exceed what can be managed within the assessment process, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) may introduce limits on the number of applications that can be submitted. Further details will be clearly communicated where this is the case. UKRI encourages organisations to support applicants in preparing well-planned, high-quality applications that are competitive for funding relative to the funding opportunity.
Aim
Curiosity-driven social science generates ideas, perspectives and breakthroughs that advance and reshape understanding, creating the foundations for future social and economic benefit. Explore awards support individuals and small teams with ambitious ideas, recognising the important role they play in generating novel questions and disruptive thinking. We welcome creative, innovative and bold proposals from anywhere within ESRC’s remit that advance knowledge by pushing disciplinary, methodological or conceptual boundaries, or otherwise generate important new understanding.
Scope
We are looking for applications that challenge assumptions, open up new areas of enquiry or new sources or uses of evidence, bring concepts together in unexpected ways, or test novel approaches and methods. Working in this way brings the potential for high reward but also involves uncertainty and risk. Outcomes may be uncertain, timelines to impact may be long-term, and the risk of failure is inherent in pushing the boundaries of social science. We are looking for ideas that embrace this challenge, take responsible risks that are integral to maximising potential, and actively manage uncertainty in ways that do not suppress innovation. Ambitious research will not always deliver anticipated results, but we expect you to demonstrate that the potential gains justify the risks involved.
What a high-quality project looks like will differ based on the focus of its ambition for advancing knowledge. You have the freedom to propose the approach best suited to achieving your aims, whether that means a research project, data resource or infrastructure initiative, or another mechanism. Projects may focus on experimental or theoretical work without a specific use in mind or be more applied in nature. We welcome proposals across a wide range of funding scales and award durations. What defines an Explore award is not the form of the project or the type of research, but the novelty and ambition of its contribution within or beyond its field, and its potential to shift understanding and inspire future directions for research.
Duration
The duration of this award is a maximum of 60 months.
Funding available
The FEC of your project can be between £300,000 and £2 million.
ESRC will fund 80% of the FEC.
What we will fund
You have wide scope and freedom to propose the research activities best suited to achieving your project’s objectives. Activities may include, but are not limited to:
basic or applied research projects
exploratory or early-stage investigations
methodological development or innovation
large-scale surveys
data infrastructure or novel data resources
secondary analysis and other forms of existing data reuse
You must clearly set out your overall objectives, your project’s novelty and potential significance, and why the proposed activities are appropriate to deliver these. You must also clearly address the risks in your proposed approach and how you plan to proactively and proportionately manage these to balance delivery, innovation and scope for long-term impact.
You are expected to set out leadership and management structures appropriate for the level of funding and type of activity you are seeking support for in the ‘Approach’ and ’Applicant and team capability to deliver’ sections.
What we will not fund
Applications cannot be accepted under this funding opportunity for:
uninvited resubmissions of projects that have previously been submitted to UKRI. Find out more about UKRI’s resubmissions policy
unspecified research work
research already underway or carried out
consultancy, evaluation or analysis whose primary purpose is to deliver pre-defined or specified policy, commercial or implementation outcomes
data collection or data resource development that substantially duplicates existing data resources without a compelling justification of the additional value it would provide
writing up previous research or completing previously funded research objectives
literature reviews
general conference attendance not related to the proposed project
travel for general study not related to the proposed project
expeditions not related to the proposed project
requests to hold conferences, workshops or seminars where these constitute the primary project component
preparation of books and publications where these constitute the primary project component
preparation and production of materials such as curriculum materials and software development where these constitute the primary project component
The following cannot be included in applications:
flexible funding pots that enable subcontracting of further small research projects
Research ethics
We require that the research we support is designed and conducted in such a way that it meets ethical principles and is subject to proper professional and institutional oversight in terms of research governance. We have agreed a Framework for Research Ethics that all submitted proposals must comply with. Read further details about the Framework for Research Ethics and guidance on compliance.
ESRC data infrastructure
We support a range of data infrastructure. You must carefully consider how your project can use, build on or contribute to existing data resources and infrastructures where appropriate. See Facilities and resources for information on finding and using ESRC datasets which are available across the UK.
Data requirements
We recognise the importance of data quality and provenance. Data generated, collected or acquired by ESRC-funded research must be well-managed by the grant holder to enable their data to be exploited to the maximum potential for further research. See our research data policy for details and further information on data requirements . The requirements of the research data policy are a condition of ESRC research funding.
Where relevant, details on data management and sharing should be provided in the Data Management section. See the importance of managing and sharing data and content for inclusion in a data management plan on the UK Data Service (UKDS) website for further guidance. We expect applicants to provide a summary of the points provided. The UKDS (email: datasharing@ukdataservice.ac.uk ) will be pleased to advise you on the availability of data within the academic community and provide advice on data deposit requirements.
Supporting skills and talent
We encourage you to follow the principles of the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers and the Technician Commitment .
Equitable partnership principles
When undertaking research and innovation activities outside the UK, you must recognise and address the possible impact of contextual, societal and cultural differences on the ethical conduct of those activities.
Researchers should also follow the principles of equitable partnerships to address inherent power imbalances when working with partners in resource-poor settings.
Applying the principles will encourage equitable access, especially in low and middle-income countries, while maintaining incentives for innovation. You should consider the principles from the start of the research and development cycle.
Read UKRI’s guidance on research in a global setting .
Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I)
UKRI is committed in ensuring that effective international collaboration in research and innovation takes place with integrity and within strong ethical frameworks. Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I) is a UKRI work programme designed to help protect all those working in our thriving and collaborative international sector by enabling partnerships to be as open as possible, and as secure as necessary. Our TR&I Principles set out UKRI’s expectations of organisations funded by UKRI in relation to due diligence for international collaboration.
As such, applicants for UKRI funding may be asked to demonstrate how their proposed projects will comply with our approach and expectation towards TR&I, identifying potential risks and the relevant controls you will put in place to help proportionately reduce these risks.
See further guidance and information about TR&I , including where you can find additional support.
How to apply
We are running this funding opportunity on the new UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Funding Service, so please ensure that your organisation is registered. You cannot apply on the Joint Electronic Submissions (Je-S) system. We will publish full details on how to apply when the funding opportunity opens.
Institutional matched funding
There is no requirement for matched funding from the institutions hosting the project lead, project co-leads or other staff employed on the application, beyond the standard 20% FEC. Expert reviewers and panels assessing UKRI funding applications must not consider levels of institutional matched funding as a factor on which to base recommendations. Direct and in-kind contributions from third party project partners are encouraged.
This policy does not remove the need for support from host organisations who must provide the necessary research environment and infrastructure for award-specific activities funded by UKRI. For example, research facilities, training and development of staff.

confirmation you have their agreement where required

Trusted Research and Innovation (TR&I)
Trusted Research and Innovation is the protection of the UK’s intellectual property, sensitive research, people, and infrastructure from potential theft, misuse, and exploitation.
Organisations receiving UKRI funding are obliged to act in line with UK government legislation. They are also expected to undertake appropriate due diligence assessment of organisations involved in research partnerships, collaboration agreements, and commercial contracts.
You will be asked about:
which areas of the National Security and Investment (NSI) Act your project relates to
who you intend to collaborate with and how
if your project requires an export control licence
Your answers may affect the T&Cs of your funding agreement if you are successful. We may use your answers to determine that our current T&Cs are sufficient or if additional T&Cs are required.
How we will assess your application
Assessment process
We will assess your application using the following process.
Eligibility checks will be carried out by ESRC at the point of submission on applicants, named staff and the application’s fit to the funding opportunity criteria. Applications which do not meet these will be rejected.
We will invite at least three expert reviewers to independently assess each application on its own merit against the funding opportunity criteria. These may be drawn from the ESRC Peer Review College or other sources. You will not be able to nominate reviewers. If your application does not receive sufficient support in scores or comments from the first two reviews it may be rejected before a third review is sourced.
If your application secures sufficient support from expert reviewers, you will be able to respond to the reviewer comments. Your application will then be considered by an appropriate ESRC applicant-led moderating panel. Panel members will use your application, the expert reviews and your response to confirm its quality against the funding opportunity requirements and provide a final score. Applications will be assessed on individual merit and will not be ranked relative to each other.
ESRC will make the final funding decision, using a tiered approach. The final funding decision may adopt a portfolio approach to ensure a diverse range of projects in accordance with  How we make decisions ; balancing novelty, research significance, approach and impact potential in a way that is appropriate to the funding opportunity aims.
We reserve the right to adapt our assessment process should we receive a large volume of applications.
Timescale
You should apply when your application is ready for submission. We will hold regular decision points and will initiate the assessment process once an application is received, ensuring you receive a timely decision.
Feedback
Applications will receive expert reviewer comments as feedback. Additional feedback will not be available. For applications that proceed to panel, the score range will be available on our website once the decisions for the opportunity have been processed fully.
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco declaration on research assessment and recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Find out about the UKRI principles of assessment and decision making .
Using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in expert review
Generative AI may only be used for the purpose of language refinement during application assessment. When using generative AI to refine the language of a review, expert reviewers and panellists must ensure that:
no part of the application being assessed is entered into a generative AI tool
no personal information from the application is disclosed
generative AI is not tasked with understanding, summarising or evaluating the application’s content
Expert reviewers and panellists must also:
comply with relevant intellectual property and data protection legislation
not take into account or speculate within their assessment whether generative AI has been used to develop the application
For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI .
Assessment areas
The assessment areas we will use are:
vision
approach
applicant and team capability to deliver
ethics and responsible research and innovation (RRI)
resources and cost justification
data management and sharing
Find details of assessment questions and criteria under the ‘Application questions’ heading in the ‘How to apply’ section.
